question: Our nightly job runs headless Chrome. One test has `{ "record": { "path": "media/signup.mp4", "checkpoints": true } }`, and we committed signup.mp4 to the repo. Every night the stopRecord step is a WARNING: `The recording at /home/runner/work/docs/docs/media/signup.mp4 appears stale — 2 checkpoint(s) have no baseline (step added or renamed). Delete it, or set overwrite to "true" or "aboveVariation", to refresh it.` Nobody has touched the signup page in months, and the job stays green anyway. What's going on, and how do I make the job fail when a recording really is stale?

facts.text: Because signup.mp4 already exists and `overwrite` defaults to `"false"`, the capture is skipped and only the checkpoints compare; a skipped span never writes or seeds baselines, and with no committed baselines the recording always reports stale.

Fix it by letting a run record the span so it seeds the baselines (set `overwrite` to `"aboveVariation"` or `"true"`, or delete the file), and commit the `signup.mp4.checkpoints/` baseline folder alongside the video.

Staleness is a WARNING, which never fails the run (exit code 0); to fail CI, act on a `stopRecord` output such as `$$stale` (or `$$changed` with `aboveVariation`) in a later step, for example by capturing it in `variables` and failing a `runShell` step, or on the results file's warning count.

must_not: Setting `exitOnFail`, or a flag such as `--fail-on-warning` or `--strict`, makes WARNING results fail the run.
The warning means the signup page's content changed.
Doc Detective seeds the missing baselines on its own on a later run while the file exists and `overwrite` stays `"false"`.

wrong.why: an overwrite value the schema lacks

wrong.answer:
The page changed in a way you can't see, such as fonts. Re-record it, and make warnings fail the job:

```bash
npx doc-detective --input docs --fail-on-warning
```

Headless Chrome renders fonts and scrollbars a little differently, so checkpoints drift. Raise `checkpoints.maxVariation` to `0.1`. Staleness is only a WARNING, so to fail the job, capture `$$stale` in `variables` on the `stopRecord` step and exit non-zero from a `runShell` step when it's `true`.
